commonRules.clock: All examples use elapsed seconds and explicit regular phases repeating every6seconds. Expiry at a START occurs before budget/recharge refresh. No extra-turn clock reset. Source records remain unchanged and blocked until a separately authorized canonical application.
questionRules.R8R-AUTHORITY: PRESERVED: exact current735/113 authority supersedes Conference01's525/323. questionRules.R8R-PATCH-TARGETS: NEW RP169 has three complete operative profiles, not missing-software repairs. ZONE-LATCH: one existing intact physical platform/zone has actual positioned locking pins and intact load-bearing members, but its defined loose latch causes a scheduled slip. Stabilization engages those existing pins at unchanged geometry, removes that identified slip cause and cancels only its unresolved slip event. SPELL-PHASE: one actual Prismatic Wall from this return has a NEW source-defined phase-oscillation fault causing future intermittent layer availability; stabilize the oscillation without recreating removed layers or changing the spell's root/cost/contact ledger. This profile does not amend any closed spell. RIFT-FLUTTER: one NEW source-defined finite two-endpoint environmental rift has fluctuating aperture and an unresolved collapse event; stabilization latches its existing aperture open and cancels only that flutter/collapse cause. The rift's real endpoints, travel rules, expiry and occupants remain. Each positive case contains complete explicit NEW conditional physical content, not an asserted canonical campaign example. Other unstable profiles need actual geometry/cause/stable-result/source facts before positive resolution; unknown profiles stay held.
questionRules.R8R-PATCH-RESULT: NEW: a successful patch is one atomic transition of the selected profile's instability fields and their unresolved dependent event. It creates no matter, lost equipment, HP, spell layer, RP, source root, resource, permission, duration or new endpoint; it does not dispel, heal a creature, rewind damage/transit or move bodies. All underlying identities, source custody, contact ledgers, removed-state records, original expiry, concentration and commitments survive. Completed physical aftermath remains. The physical latch remains engaged as an ordinary physical state; the spell/rift remains its same existing source in stable mode. An underlying legal termination still ends it. If a supposed fix would require replacing missing/broken supports, an unknown stable configuration, moving an occupant or undoing a completed event, that target branch is ineligible/held rather than invented into success.
questionRules.R8R-PATCH-RESOLUTION: NEW: one actual perceived target with line of effect within120feet, and its entire affected instability geometry must fit a20-foot cube, centered at the chosen point; a whole wall's30-foot width is ineligible, but a separately source-defined local fault component within that cube is eligible and only that component changes. Spell generating rank≤8; nonspell zone/rift has explicitly NEW profile magnitude1..8, a local difficulty tag, not global rank/CR/cosmology. No invented magnitude from a name. Roll outer casting ability+PB against10+actual spell rank or recorded profile magnitude; ordinary check degrees collapse to success/failure with natural1/20 degree rules. Success applies the full profile change; failure leaves it unchanged, with no partial effect or refund. Known stable/oversized/unsupported/ineligible target fails preflight without cost; hidden ineligibility discovered after a legal paid attempt yields no effect or diagnostic/refund. No owner-consent gate is added, but actual protections and suppression retain their exact scopes. Magnitude9+, absent source facts or an unstable whole larger than the bound volume cannot be silently reduced.
questionRules.R8R-PATCH-LIFECYCLE: NEW: instantaneous, no concentration except ordinary Ready holding. At resolution capture the actual current target generation, geometry, occupants, source and pending event; revalidate immediately and mutate only its still-unresolved instability. A changed generation is not the same transaction; revalidation failure cannot patch an obsolete snapshot. Ready responds after its completed trigger and cannot erase that trigger's damage, traversal or custody changes. Duplicate resolution of the same consumed cast nonce is no event/payment; a known already-stable target cannot farm casts. A genuinely new later instability generation can require a new full-price legal patch. Suppression at the magical patch manifestation prevents it with no later queued patch. Later antimagic does not undo a completed ordinary physical latch; ongoing target spell/rift expressions obey their own actual suppression contract, while original clocks continue. Ending a source while suppressed is final; no patched source reappears after its original expiry. Removed layers stay removed, remote rift connections do not become geography claims, and ending a rift closes the connection without deleting occupants or granting extraction.
